items.title: Show HN: I built a Bible verse feed to replace doomscrolling (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hey all, I just released my latest iOS app, Scroll Hope. It is a tiktok like scrolling feed, but the content is Bible verses with fun dynamic backgrounds. It also tracks your reading progress and keeps stats over time. You can try it out on the website, or on iOS if you want the app lockout feature which lets you block your social apps. Completely free, with the option to support the app with a tip and unlock some additional icon and sharing options. Coming soon is audio and auto-scroll, so you can set the phone down and read/listen hands free. Android is on the way, the lockout feature is taking some additional review time. items.title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. No need to answer every question of course, just wanted to get a gut feel how people are using AI. 1) What AI subscriptions are you personally paying for? (Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor, etc) - Which tiers? - Have you purchased multiple subscriptions from the same provider (eg two Claude accounts)? 2) Are you using models outside (or instead) of those subscriptions? For example, pay-as-you-go APIs, OpenRouter, or locally hosted models. - Which models and providers? 3) What coding harnesses and interfaces are you using? Are you sticking with the default CLIs or IDE integrations, or using alternatives like OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Muse Code, or custom-built harnesses? - What made you switch harnesses (if you switched)? 4) Are you using any agent orchestration or swarm tools? - For example, Munder Difflin, Gas Town, Ruflo, or something custom. 5) Are you using broader agent platforms like OpenClaw / Hermes Agent / Grok bot / Dots / Muse? - If you are using them, what are your main use cases? ----- I know my workflow has differed significantly from a year ago, and so it would be interesting to capture a snapshot today of what people are using and why. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50366117 Points: 21 # Comments: 10

items.title: Tell HN: Gemini trains on chat history, even for subscribers (personal accounts) (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: If you have a personal Google AI subscription, all your saved chat history in Gemini can be used for training and there is no way to opt out unless you turn off chat history or use temporary chat sessions. These chat transcripts may even be read by human reviewers. Although Google claims to disconnect them from your account when human-reviewed, they explicitly warn not to enter confidential information. https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16836988 "[Gemini app activity] is used to improve Google services for everyone, including by training generative AI models, if your Keep Activity setting is on." https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#human_review "A subset of chats are reviewed by human reviewers" https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#pn_retain_data "Chats reviewed by human reviewers [...] are not deleted when you delete your activity. Instead, they are retained for up to three years." https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961?hl=en#pn_data_usage "Please don't enter confidential information that you wouldn't want a reviewer to see or Google to use to improve our services, including machine-learning technologies." To disable their training on your chat sessions, you need to turn off "Keep Activity" in Gemini's settings. Turning that off means you'll lose any chat sessions after 72 hours. I learned this too late, thinking that having a paid subscription = not being turned into the product. Apparently paying is not enough. Thank you to this user on HN for mentioning in another thread: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50355424 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50363461 Points: 350 # Comments: 96
